lines: I do not have a trade for that sort of night. I survived it anyway.
I found a corner, then a path, then home. That is more plan than I started with.
I made it back without a trade, a plan, or much dignity. Still counts.
My legs only started shaking after I reached the gate.
The sound of home after fighting nearly broke me.
Some wounds waited until I felt safe enough to notice them.
Leaving while I still could was the smartest thing I did.
Fear stayed close through the whole battle.
The first quiet moment afterward felt louder than the fight.
I kept walking because stopping did not feel possible.
Making it home counts even if nobody looked brave doing it.
I used a doorway, a wall, and better luck than I deserved.
I can help repair the damage after I sleep.
I did not win the fight. I survived it.
The gate looked farther away every time I stumbled.
Someone took my arm on the last stretch. I never asked who.
I learned that retreat can be the right choice.
I am sore in places I did not know could be sore.
Tomorrow I will help count damage. Tonight I need rest.
Home is enough victory for me.
